rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and reveal the overall retention window and any obvious critical pairs. This balances coverage and run time while reducing the risk of an uninformative truncated first run.

All pairs are fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing t_last by steepening the gradient. Keep phi0, phi1, and T fixed and shorten tG one step to test how much run time can be cut before the 6/7 region begins to lose resolution.

Resolution is still complete and the limiting pair is only modestly above 1.5, so take one more step steeper to try to bring the last peak under 10 min. This directly tests whether we can reach the maximum CRF before the 6/7 pair falls below threshold.

At tG 14 the only issue is the 6/7 pair, while time is already optimal with t_last under 10 min. Lowering temperature one step should increase retention and improve selectivity/resolution for that critical cluster with only a modest risk of pushing the last peak back above 10 min.

The 35 C test worsened selectivity in the crowded middle, so probe the opposite direction: raising temperature at the same fast gradient may improve the critical 6/7 separation while keeping t_last below 10 min. This is the quickest way to see whether temperature can recover full resolution at tG 14 and reach CRF 1.0.

Higher temperature at tG 14 compressed the critical region too much, so increase gradient time one step while keeping T at 45 C to see whether faster mass transfer plus a slightly shallower slope restores full resolution with t_last still near or under 10 min. This tests whether temperature and slope can be traded to beat the current best at 16 min, 40 C.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead narrow the gradient window slightly to reduce the effective slope in the crowded elution region. This may recover the 6/7 resolution at the fast 14 min gradient while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

Narrowing the gradient window improved the critical 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This should further reduce the effective slope around the crowded middle and may lift the last sub-1.5 pair to full credit without sacrificing the time term.

At phi1 0.85 and 14 min all pairs are resolved but the last peak is slightly too late, so shorten tG one step to pull t_last back under 10 min. This tests whether full resolution can be maintained at the narrower window and should be the most direct route to CRF 1.0.

The best region is between the fully resolved but slightly slow 0.85/14 method and the fast but slightly under-resolved 0.90/14 method. Increasing tG to 16 min at phi1 0.90 should preserve full resolution and may place t_last near 10 min, potentially improving on the current best.

The best methods suggest the optimum may come from keeping the narrower window but shifting the whole gradient slightly stronger at the start to pull late compounds earlier while preserving local slope near the critical middle cluster. Raising phi0 by one step is a targeted way to try to keep 6/7 at or above 1.5 while maintaining t_last under 10 min.

The phi0 increase improved time while keeping the same critical pair behavior, so now combine it with the narrower upper endpoint that previously restored full resolution. This is the most promising nearby condition for reaching full resolution with t_last still under 10 min.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so the sensible next move is to test whether the method can be made faster while maintaining all pairs at R >= 1.5. Shortening tG by one step directly probes whether the current optimum has any excess resolution margin.

Since shortening tG lost resolution, keep the successful 14 min slope but raise phi0 one step to see if the run can be made earlier without compressing the critical pair too much. This explores whether a stronger starting composition can retain full resolution while moving t_last safely below 10 min.

The move to phi0 0.15 preserved full resolution and improved speed, so continue one more step stronger at the start while keeping the same successful upper endpoint and gradient time. This checks whether we can further shorten the method without sacrificing the critical 6/7 pair.

Phi0 0.15 gave full resolution with margin, so keep that stronger start and narrow the upper endpoint one more step to reduce slope around the critical region. This may retain full resolution while still keeping the run at or below the current 9.6 min last peak.

At phi1 0.80 and tG 14 all pairs are safely resolved but the run is slightly too long, indicating excess resolution margin in the critical region. Shortening tG by one step is the best test for a faster fully resolved method that could still keep CRF at the maximum.

We already have CRF 1.0, so use remaining budget to seek a potentially faster equally optimal method around the best condition. Raising temperature one step from the robust phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85, tG 14 setting may pull the last peak earlier while the existing resolution margin might still keep the critical pair above 1.5.

Temperature sensitivity is strong, so use a remaining injection to map the opposite corner around the successful method: lower T but compensate with a longer gradient. This checks whether cooler conditions can give a more robust fully resolved method, even if CRF is unlikely to beat the current maxima.

Use the remaining budget to probe another nearby tradeoff at 40 C: a wider window but shorter gradient than the successful 0.15/0.85/14 method. This will help confirm the local optimum boundary for the critical 6/7 pair and may reveal an equally optimal but shorter-program method.

This is the remaining untested corner between two known maxima: 0.10/0.85/14 and 0.15/0.80/14 are both fully resolved, so 0.10/0.80/14 may also retain full resolution while shifting the timing balance. With a few injections left, this is the most informative nearby check around the optimum plateau.

A wider upper endpoint combined with the stronger start at phi0 0.15 is the last nearby 40 C condition that could plausibly stay fully resolved while shifting the late peak timing. This completes the local map around the optimum ridge and checks whether the 1.0 solution extends to a faster high-phi1 variant.

With the optimum already found, use a remaining run to define the safe fully resolved side of the design space by lengthening the successful 0.10/0.85 method. This should preserve full resolution with extra margin and helps confirm that the 14 min method is near the shortest fully resolved condition.

One useful untested point remains on the 40 C map: the lowest phi0 with the narrowest successful window. This checks the other edge of the optimum region and helps confirm how strongly the starting composition, rather than just window width, controls the critical 6/7 separation.

For the final run, test the last nearby 40 C corner combining the stronger start that shortened the run with the narrower window that improved 6/7 resolution. It is unlikely to beat the two established 1.0 methods, but it completes the local optimum map and could still reveal another fully resolved sub-10 min variant.
